Five pkg.go.dev public package-search queries yielded 321 hits and 228 unique package paths. The png, png decoder, and image png result windows each stopped at 100; png reader yielded 12 and png parser yielded 9. The HTML search pages do not provide an overall total, so none is inferred. Five named documentation leads remain unresolved and eligible parsers may lie outside these windows. Several packages wrap or fork Go image/png and two use libvips, so 20 package paths do not imply 20 independent engines. One pinned TinyGo PNG decoder panicked on the valid control and is excluded. The one 2×1 pixel control only proves the observed parsing path. Package-level importer counts are adoption signals, not downloads, and absent values are not inferred.

Five pkg.go.dev public package-search queries saved 333 hits and 271 unique package paths. The zip, archive zip, and unzip result pages were truncated at 100 each; zip reader returned 23 and zip parser returned 10. The HTML pages did not expose a total result count, so none is inferred. 8 named plausible leads remain unresolved. Search hits are discovery material, not parser evidence, and eligible packages may exist outside these windows. Many verified packages wrap or fork Go archive/zip, so 23 package paths do not imply 23 independent engines. One pinned itchio/arkive ZIP reader passed the control but lacked open-source license evidence and was excluded. The shared one-entry DEFLATE control does not cover other ZIP features. Importer counts are package-level adoption signals from pkg.go.dev at one snapshot date; missing values are not invented.

Five pkg.go.dev public package-search queries saved 133 hits and 124 unique package paths. Query windows returned 100, 10, 11, 12, 0 hits in order; the broad mp4 window stopped at 100. The HTML pages give no total result count, so none is inferred. Ten plausible leads remain unresolved, including readers for fragmented MP4 that require a different valid control. Search hits are leads, not evidence. Several verified packages share mp4ff, joy4, gomedia, jfbus, or dhowden/tag code lineages, so the package count does not imply independent parser engines. A single progressive isom MP4 with two tracks and a title proves only the labeled API paths. Importer counts are pkg.go.dev package-level adoption signals, not downloads; zero means no visible direct importers in this snapshot.

Five pkg.go.dev public package-search queries saved 373 hits and 271 unique paths. The wav and wav decoder result windows each stopped at 100; wave audio, riff wav, and wav reader returned 72, 73, and 28. The HTML pages give no total result count, so none is inferred. Eight named plausible leads remain unresolved; other eligible packages may fall outside these windows. Several included packages share beep or mattetti/go-audio WAV lineage. One valid four-sample PCM16 control establishes only the listed parse path, and cryptix/wav is counted on its header and sample-count output because its sample sign disagreed with the control. pkg.go.dev direct-importer counts are package-level adoption signals rather than downloads; no missing metrics are invented.

Five npm queries each saved only the first 100 results from much larger result sets; 372 unique hits are discovery material, not all investigated. 15 named plausible leads remain unresolved. More qualified parsers may exist outside these search windows. The 20 verified package names include narrow ftyp/header parsers and metadata readers and need not represent 20 independent full-media decoders. The control checks one small H.264/AAC file with fixed tags, and the browser result applies to one pinned Chromium build. mp4-metadata requires a FileReader compatibility shim in Node; its parser itself reads the supplied Blob.

Five npm queries saved 495 hits (the id3v2 query returned only 95), covering 447 unique names. Four query result sets were truncated at 100; hits are not all investigated and qualified packages may exist beyond these windows. 10 named plausible leads remain unresolved. Verified packages include tag-only parsers, duration readers, MP3 decoders, and wrappers over shared music-metadata, node-id3, or mpg123 implementations. Duration APIs report different values because of encoder delay/padding, so the expected result is package-specific and recorded. The single control covers ID3v2.3 with three text fields and a one-second tone, not all ID3 or MP3 variants. Browser APIs do not expose tags.

PyPI has no public relevance-ranked keyword search API in this workflow, so the Simple JSON project index was filtered by seven name substrings. The filters matched 210, 21, 19, 71, 143, 14, and 54 project names respectively; the first 100 case-insensitive alphabetical matches were saved per filter, 379 distinct names in total. Alphabetical windows can miss relevant and highly adopted packages, so project documentation supplied additional leads. Eight plausible leads remain unresolved, including a PNG decoder without a macOS wheel, a headless loader that could not import, and packages requiring separate environments. Several accepted packages delegate to Pillow, ImageIO, libvips, or other native engines; 21 package paths do not mean 21 independent decoder engines. The two valid controls prove only the labeled pixel, header, chunk, or tEXt scopes. Tkinter PhotoImage is verified separately on bundled Tk 8.6 and may be absent in other Python distributions. PyPI Stats downloads are a within-Python adoption proxy; byteparse returned HTTP 404 for this metric and remains unranked.

The PyPI Simple JSON project index was filtered by nine package-name substrings, retaining up to 100 case-insensitive alphabetical hits per term. The 418 saved hits contain 407 distinct names but are not a popularity search; relevant packages outside the windows may be missed. Six plausible leads remain unresolved, including the high-download zipfile-deflate64 whose source build failed on this macOS ARM/Python 3.13 host. The 20 verified distribution paths include many wrappers/backports over CPython zipfile; they are not 20 independent ZIP engines. The Zstandard reader was tested on a valid method-93 ZIP made by a pinned generator; other packages used the one-entry DEFLATE control. One entry is a local archive extractor backed by an external unzip utility, recorded as such. The four separate standard-library APIs share underlying ZIP code. Each control proves only its stated compression method, member, and API scope.

The PyPI Simple JSON project index was filtered by 12 name substrings. The first 100 case-insensitive alphabetical matches per filter were saved, yielding 675 hits and 669 unique names; name windows have no popularity ordering and can miss relevant packages. Project docs supplied additional candidates. Six plausible leads remain unresolved, including source-only/native bindings and generic image readers. The 20 verified distribution paths include 18 P3 pixel readers, one P2 pixel reader, and one P3 dimensions-only reader; several share Pillow, Qt, or netpbmfile parser families. The local bundled Tk 8.6 PhotoImage API rejected valid P1/P2/P3 controls despite broad official PPM/PGM documentation, so no standard API is counted for this ASCII cell. PyPI Stats initially rate-limited one request; a later successful retry supplied its within-Python download metric.
